---
title: "AI Use in DSA105"
---

## Principle

AI tools may support learning, but they must not replace the student's first attempt at computational reasoning.

The default rule is:

> **Think first → produce something → ask AI → verify always**

## Before using an AI assistant

Produce at least one of the following yourself:

- a problem representation;
- pseudocode;
- a prediction;
- a partial implementation;
- a test case;
- an error diagnosis.

## Acceptable learning roles

AI may be used for:

- explanation;
- debugging support;
- syntax/code completion;
- alternative solutions;
- comparison of implementations.

When AI use is part of a homework task, you may be asked to state:

- what you had produced before asking AI;
- what you accepted;
- what you rejected or changed;
- how you verified the result.

## Why verification matters

A program can run and still be logically wrong.  
An AI-generated solution can be syntactically correct and still misunderstand the problem.

Your responsibility is therefore not only to obtain code, but to understand and test the computational behaviour.
